VOID ARMOR: FORM DRIVE is a top-down mech action shooter built around short combat missions, pre-mission loadout customization, real-time weapon FORM switching, and performance-based mission rankings.

Take control of the experimental mech ARORA and engage a variety of enemy machines across multiple missions.

Before each mission, customize your loadout by selecting equipment within your available capacity. Choose from weapons and systems such as the Rifle, Shotgun, Charge Rifle, Launcher, Energy Blade, and Defense System, and build a loadout that suits your preferred playstyle.

During combat, switch between your equipped weapon FORMs in real time. Close the distance with the Energy Blade, attack from range with rifles and launchers, or use the Defense System to withstand incoming fire. Choosing the right FORM for each situation is key to surviving battle.

After each mission, your performance is evaluated based on factors such as clear time, damage taken, and accuracy. Defeat enemies quickly and precisely while minimizing damage to earn a higher rank.

Features

  • CUSTOM LOADOUT

Before each mission, select your equipment within the available capacity limit. Focus on offensive power, add defensive options, or improve mobility to create a loadout that matches your playstyle.

  • REAL-TIME WEAPON FORM SWITCHING

Switch between your equipped weapons and systems during battle. Adapt between close-range combat, ranged attacks, and defensive options depending on the situation.

  • FAST-PACED TOP-DOWN COMBAT

Move with WASD, aim with the mouse, and react to enemy mech attacks in real time.

  • DIFFICULTY SELECTION

In EASY mode, a slow-motion effect activates when enemies fire, giving you more time to react. NORMAL mode removes this slowdown for faster and more intense combat.

  • Mission-based single-player gameplay

Clear short combat missions and aim for better results through repeated attempts.

  • Performance-based ranking

Clear time, damage taken, accuracy, and other results affect your final rank.

VOIDHOLD is a sci-fi horde-survival roguelite. You command a four-soldier fireteam — VECTOR, NOVA and ECHO at your side, the combat dog REX-7 and the eagle-drone AQUILA in support — holding a position at the edge of the void against waves that never stop escalating.

COMMAND A FIRETEAM


  • You are the commander. Three AI troopers fight beside you, named and colour-coded, gaining veteran strength every level — and the comms track the fight: arrival calls on every world, first-contact warnings, allies down.

  • Two companions field with you: REX-7, a combat dog, and AQUILA, a recon eagle-drone.

  • Hold Q — the left bumper on a controller — to open the command wheel: order the whole squad, companions included, to engage freely, protect you, hold a position or focus one target. They still move, aim and fire on their own.

  • Fallen troopers and companions redeploy when you reach the next planet. Losses are a setback you carry through the world, not a run-ender.

ENDLESS, ESCALATING


  • Ten distinct biomes, looping endlessly. The horde grows level after level — a felled boss buys one breather before it climbs again — and every planet fields its own flavour of the horde.

  • A mini-boss holds the middle of every biome and a boss caps it — two different foes from five rotating archetypes: a demon bruiser, a green zone-caster, a charging juggernaut, an aerial dive-bomber, an ice brute-king. Each is a telegraphed weak-point fight, never an HP sponge.

  • How deep can you hold? A local high-score board keeps every run honest, and Steam leaderboards rank your best unbroken run against your friends and the whole world.

BUILD-CRAFTING SYNERGIES

  • Every run is a different build. Seven mods — HOLLOW-POINT, SIPHON ROUNDS, ARC CONDUCTOR, KILL-DRIVE, AEGIS CORE, INCENDIARY, ADRENALINE — combine into 23 named synergies, among them EXECUTE, GLASS CANNON, CHAIN REACTION, SCORCHED EARTH, THERMAL CORE, BLOODLUST, VAMPIRE, APEX PREDATOR, MELTDOWN, BERSERKER, FRENZY, JUGGERNAUT, LAST STAND and FORTRESS.

  • Every run banks SALVAGE. Spend it across seven PROGRAMS for permanent starting edges: credits, a pre-fitted jetpack, charged shields, reinforced hull, weapon logistics, REX-7 and AQUILA.

HOLD THE LINE


  • Tight third-person, over-the-shoulder shooting with weight, recoil and kill-juice.

  • Six weapons on one arm-cannon — carbine, piercing breaker, plasma lance, scatter, charge-railgun, incendiary — swapped freely mid-fight.

  • A cohesive neon sci-fi look, an original driving electronic soundtrack, zero telemetry.

FEATURES

  • A four-soldier fireteam, each trooper with a distinct weapon, plus a combat dog and a recon drone

  • A four-order command wheel for the whole squad, on keyboard or controller

  • Endless escalation across ten looping biomes — per-planet horde flavours, mutated variants, rule-twist wave events

  • Roguelite synergy builds — 23 named combos from seven mods

  • Six free-swap weapons, from carbine to charge-railgun to incendiary

  • Five rotating boss archetypes — a mini-boss and a boss in every biome, each a telegraphed weak-point check

  • A high-score chase — local board plus friends and global Steam leaderboards — and 31 Steam achievements, from FIRST STAND to the 5,000-kill chain

  • Eight medal-graded challenge OPERATIONS, each on its own world, from the boss-rush GAUNTLET to the OMEGA PROTOCOL capstone

  • Boundary saves with an ironman record — SAVE RUN between worlds; only unbroken runs enter the board

  • Single-player, with full controller support and rebindable keys

The VPet shop just got its biggest delivery ever — and every single toy is on the floor.

VPet Sort Together is a cozy organizing simulator about a pastel virtual pet toy shop. Pick up egg keychains, boxed pets, watches, rings, necklaces and silicone jackets, find the display each one belongs to, and watch the chaos turn into perfectly sorted shelves. Play alone at your own pace, or invite up to three friends and tidy up together.

Sort thousands of tiny pets

Over 9,600 toys fill a shop of 8 islands and 135 displays. 120 different products — each a colourway, a pet and a kind, like the Mint Polka Avoki Keychain — wait for their slot on pegboards, egg carton tables, watch towers, ring bars, necklace trees and cubby walls.

Better together

Online co-op for 1–4 players through a Steam lobby. Split the departments, race each other to the last empty hook, or just throw everything at your friends. There is no time limit — the shop is done when you say it is.

Toss, stack and carry

Throw a toy straight onto its display, carry a whole stack in your tote bag and snap it into place. Upgrade your paws in the skill tree — Pet Radar, Display Finder, Quick Paws, Perfect Toss, Big Tote Bag, Speedy Steps and more — and grab perks from the Giant VPet vendor.

Six departments, one very cute shop

Egg Keychains, Boxed Pets, Watches, Rings, Necklaces and Silicone Jackets — each department has its own displays, colours and 16 pixel pets living on tiny LCD screens: Avoki, Crackle, Blinky, Grumble, Wobble, Boo, Sparky and friends.

Cozy details

  • A glossy pastel shop with mirror-like floors and soft lights

  • Dress up your character at the wardrobe and pick a tune at the 8-bit boombox

  • 10 playable characters

  • No timer, no fail state — just the satisfying click of the last toy finding its home

HOW IT WORKS.

Using VTC is simple.

Hold your Push-To-Talk button, speak naturally, and VTC sends your message directly to the in-game chat.

Fast, seamless, and designed to keep you focused on the game.

PLAY YOUR WAY.

VTC works with the setup you already use.

Whether you play with a keyboard, mouse, controller or racing wheel, VTC adapts to your preferred input method.

RUNS IN THE BACKGROUND.

VTC is always ready when you need it.

Speak naturally, stay focused on the game, and keep your hands on the controls.

We travel the universe, and we bring planets back to life.

Proxima Centauri b, 2194. Your pod came down hard. The sky is thin, toxic, and dying — and the planet is still alive enough to know you are here.

You are not a colonist. You are not a conqueror. You revive worlds, and then you move on.

Build a factory out of the periodic table

Everything you mine is a real isotope. Not "ore" — carbon-12, iron-56, uranium-238, each with its own proton and neutron count, its own stability, its own way of falling apart.

  • Identify unknown minerals by their actual emission spectra, every element from hydrogen to uranium

  • Synthesize compounds in a molecular assembler that validates by real valence and oxidation states — build Fe₂O₃ and the game names it Hematite

  • Transmute elements you can't find in the ground using alpha and beta decay

  • Breed Pu-239, ignite a fission reactor, then put its own waste to work in an RTG

  • Trap positrons in a Penning trap and make antimatter

The tech tree is the periodic table. Get the chemistry wrong and the machine simply will not run.

Automate everything

Belts, inserters, filters and splitters. Refineries, assemblers, and drone logistics networks that fly cargo between chests on request. Power grids you wire pole by pole, with generation, storage and demand you have to actually balance — because every watt you draw is a watt something else can hear.

Wire a computer out of rocks

The planet's spirit speaks in signals. To hear it, you have to build senses.

The circuit kit is a complete binary logic system: AND, OR and XOR gates, memory cells, and sixty-four wireless channels. Read the planet's demands, switch entire power grids on the result, interlock your cooling against your water supply so you never freeze the sky you are trying to fill.

It is complete enough to build a working ripple-carry adder and a memory accumulator. We know, because we built both to test it.

Terraform a real atmosphere

The air is a literal inventory of gases. Pressure is how much is in it. Oxygen is what fraction of it happens to be O₂ — vent nitrogen and your oxygen percentage rises without adding a single molecule of it. Water is a gas too, freezing and thawing across a pressure-scaled frost line. Burn carbon and CO₂ enters the sky by pure stoichiometry: one atom in, one molecule out, no fudge factor.

The planet demands four seasons — each one a band on pressure, temperature, oxygen and water that you must hold all at once, until it is satisfied. Hold all four, and the world comes back.

Something is under the sand

Your factory has an electrical signature, and the sandworms can feel it. They map your base by how much power each patch of ground has ever drawn, then take the loudest one. You cannot kill them. You can only not be there when they arrive.

  • Read the seismic radar and evacuate before impact

  • Build inside ancient rock formations, where the ground goes quiet

  • Or put your entire factory on a flying platform and lift it out of the way

Then leave

There is a ship buried under five metres of wind-blown sand. Revive the world and the planet itself will tell you where to dig. Get it out, fuel it with antimatter you made with your own hands, and go.

There are other worlds waiting.

Features

  • Fully destructible voxel terrain — dig anywhere, mine anything

  • Deep factory automation: belts, inserters, filters, drones and logistics networks

  • Real science: spectroscopy, decay chains, valence bonding, fission, antimatter

  • Closed-loop terraforming over a genuine per-gas atmospheric simulation

  • A full binary logic kit for automating the planet — or building a calculator

  • Flying platforms that carry entire sections of your factory

  • Moddable — the game's data and logic live in plain, editable Lua files

Vampolitics is a narrative resource management RPG set in a dark and silly world of The SPACE VAMPIRES.

Take on the challenging role of a Space Sovereign and rule your own Space Vampire Space kingdom during the twilight years of a once powerful coven... but be warned your resources are almost gone, the nobles want you dead and your closes family members have their own ambitions.

...and worst of all your own Space Janitor is viewed more favorably by your most trusted advisers than you are.

Rule from the Throne Room

Each week, you’ll decide how best to spend your resources. Will you use your gold to upgrade the old ships from your last battle, or patron a visiting artist from another corner of the galaxy? The choice is yours as you sit upon your throne as the oddballs of the galaxy come to ask for your aid. 

Family Matters in a manner

Your family bloodline also plays a vital role in establishing your claim throughout the Space Vampire realm. Choose your starting family wisely, as some offer unique events and resources that could make or break your attempt to balance the covens books. Will you marry off a relative to the cultists to keep the peace? Trade a spouse for gold? Or perhaps attend a grand ball for the other prominent Space Vampires? The choice is yours.

Face the Strange and Unusual

Build your reputation by navigating bizarre events and difficult dilemmas. A prisoner of war might be sold, drained for blood, put to work, or kept in a cage in your throne room for your own amusement. A strange merchant might try to sell you a painted rock... or the very secrets of the cosmos. From astro-artists and doctors with brains in bowls are there to explore.

Fighters of the Void

Rebuild your coven’s fleet and notoriety. Upgrade your warships, send ships and troops to raid enemy vessels. Expand into new territories for more resources and opportunities.

Collect unique assets: including artifacts, wonders, unique people, and powerful military ships with death rays

Two Modes of Play

the two Act Story Mode introduces the main systems of Vampolitics as you try to keep your kingdom manageable and your sanity intact.

Conquest Mode is about expanding your borders, alone or with friends. Play solo or in multiplayer and see how far your coven can grow.

Vangrid is a top-down tactical shooter you can play solo or team up with friends online. Storm strongholds, hold points, escort convoys, or retake lost outposts across procedurally assembled maps where the terrain, reinforcements, and threats change every match — using firepower, drivable vehicles, and active backpack skills to turn the tide of battle.

Key Features

  • Online co-op: Team up with friends to capture points, defend, and counter-attack across multiple mission types

  • Ever-changing maps: Chunk-based map generation means every match has a different layout, approach, and threat level

  • Drivable vehicles: Tanks, helicopters, and more turn the tide of battle

  • Active backpack skills: Heal, build, repair, call in an airdrop, or call in an airstrike — mix and match to fit your playstyle

  • Logistics System: Rescue wounded soldiers and hostages, and do not let the enemy breach your defensive lines.

  • Smart AI squads: Behavior-tree-driven enemies with distinct tactical roles (assault, sniper, medic, engineer), backed by towering bosses

  • Deep loadout customization: Mix weapons, armor, and backpacks to build your own tactical kit

Ready? Rally your squad. Every inch of lost territory is waiting to be reclaimed.

OVERVIEW

Vanguard's Descent is a 3D action roguelite where you build a party of heroes, fight through branching dungeons, and combine character abilities and upgrades into powerful team synergies.

COMMAND THE VANGUARD

  • Master a combat system that blends real-time action with tactical decision-making.

  • Dodge enemy attacks and look for openings as combat unfolds in real time. Activate powerful abilities, choose your targets, and command your three-hero party.

  • Learn enemy attack patterns, time your abilities, and coordinate your heroes to defeat increasingly dangerous enemies.

BUILD A DIFFERENT TEAM EVERY RUN

  • Recruit heroes with unique combat kits and choose from multiple archetypes that change how each character plays.

  • Throughout each run, collect randomized upgrades and combine their effects to create powerful synergies between your heroes.

  • Experiment with different characters, archetypes, and upgrade combinations as you develop new strategies and push deeper into the dungeon.

EXPLORE BRANCHING DUNGEONS

  • Fight your way through a series of distinct environments, each with its own enemies, encounters, and atmosphere.

  • Choose your route through procedurally generated branching dungeons as you decide when to pursue rewards, recover your party, or take on more dangerous battles.

SAVE THE WORLD

The Plagued have consumed what remains of the world. As a member of the Vanguard, gather your team, descend into corrupted lands, and fight to eradicate the Plagued.

You are a grave robber, not a hero, not someone with good intentions. You plan to enter a legendary pyramid-shaped dungeon where each room is rumored to be a time machine to a distant extinct civilization. You enter this dungeon not to steal its gold, but to steal its history, as every civilization's final moments are clouded in mystery, and each piece of information about their end is way more valuable than any pile of gold you would find here.

  • High Replayability

Every run is procedurally assembled. The room order, the artifacts you find, and the layout of the floors are never the same twice.

  • Intense Bullet Hell Combat

Dodge intricate bullet patterns spawned by both the enemies and from the room walls themselves.

  • Each Room is Different

Every room in the dungeon represents a different extinct civilization, with its own enemies, its own theme, and its own way to help you reach to the end.

  • Powerful Upgrades

Throughout your run you will discover different artifacts that you can use to upgrade your weapon and to customize your build.

Patience is power

Vauren's BeastBorn is a competitive deck builder built entirely around combos. Plan your strategy carefully: here, the real power lies in patience.

Many effects evolve when they reach a certain number of stacks, transforming into more powerful (or completely different) versions of themselves. A modest effect played early can become the card that decides the match... if you give it time.

Spend now, or wait?

Every game is a constant decision between spending now and continuing to accumulate. Do you wait one more turn for your effect to mutate, or unleash it now before your opponent snatches it away? Every stack you hold is a promise of power, and a risk your rival can punish.

1v1, mind against mind

Face off against other players in 1v1 matches where reading the rhythm of a combo is just as important as building a good deck. Watch what your opponent is stacking, anticipate when they will strike, and choose the perfect moment to break their plan or complete your own.

A roster built for combos

  • 6 main characters, each with their own signature cards and playstyle

  • 5 secondary characters who bring unique cards to the table

  • Around 150 cards to unlock as you progress, sorted by rarity

  • 24 passives that change the way your deck plays

Free to play, ready from day one

Every character is playable from your very first match with a preset deck. Unlock new cards and passives simply by playing to build your own decks, or unlock full customization faster through optional paid DLC.

Wishlist now

Add Vauren's BeastBorn to your wishlist to be notified when the demo launches, and start planning your first combo.

"The battle to claim the last remaining island in a post-apocalyptic world begins."

It is a game about surviving to the very end

by gathering resources, securing food, and building structures.

Choosing the right location is crucial; you must decide where to make your home.

Manage your time wisely—you need to decide whether to gather resources or focus on construction.

And watch out for surprise enemy attacks.

A missing brother, a borrowed sword

Castra has always lived in the shadow of its clock tower. When a simple bounty with his friend Gill turns into a fight, Raine is summoned to Castra Castle, where his uncle Gale hands him the family sword and a writ. His brother Asperitas has vanished along with the outpost soldiers, and the trail leads into the forest. What Raine finds out there is older than Castra, and his brother may not be the same man who left.

Two ways to fight

On the field, Raine fights in real time. Slash, charge a heavy swing that throws a sword beam, and read each enemy's wind-up. Swing into the white flash and you parry: the world drops to a pencil sketch for a heartbeat while Raine and his foe stay in color, then you riposte.

Let an enemy reach you and the fight becomes a turn-based battle for the whole party. A watch-hand ring sweeps on every attack and every block; stop it in the gold for a PERFECT hit or a PERFECT guard. Enemies carry guard pips you can break to Shatter them open, they hold grudges about who hurt them, and allies can team up for dual techs.

A world that keeps its own hours

Day turns to dusk and dusk to night. Lamps come on in Castra, the forest gets darker and less friendly, and some things only hunt after sundown. Rest at campfires, take bounties off the town quest board, read the books you find, and fill in a bestiary that learns each enemy's weaknesses as you fight them. In the taverns, people will deal you into the Slog, a collectible card game with its own rivals.

Features

  • Real-time field combat with parries, charged heavies and sketch-time ripostes

  • Turn-based party battles with timed strikes and blocks, guard-breaking Shatter, enemy grudges, and dual techs

  • Hand-painted maps from Castra and its forest to snowbound mountains, a waterfall temple and blighted ruins

  • A 32-track score by composer Tim Carlos

  • Optional voiced dialogue and narrated books, more than 3,800 voiced lines (see the AI disclosure)

  • The Slog, a collectible card game with rivals across the world

  • 29 quests and bounties, 31 readable books and a 62-entry bestiary

  • 16 achievements, New Game+, and four difficulty levels from Easy to Master

  • Text speed, auto-advance, battle pacing and a visual clarity setting

Credits

Lead Programmer: Vladimir Skrypnikov (Pheonix KageDesu)

Producer: Lliam Sedawie

Game Artist: Kaue Luchetta

Music: Tim Carlos

SRPG in Search of Balance

On a continent where the ideals of three nations clash, what will you choose, and what will you defend?

Verdant Requiem is a story-driven tactical RPG that combines classic strategic gameplay with a sweeping war chronicle, branching storylines, and original military management systems.

This is not a simple tale of good versus evil.

Resources, faith, military power, and national interests all shape the conflicts of this world. As the ideals—and contradictions—of each nation clash, Leonis and his companions are drawn into a struggle over the balance of the entire continent.

What kind of future awaits this land will depend on the choices you make.

# A Full-Length, Story-Driven SRPG

*Verdant Requiem* is designed as a full-length tactical RPG, with over 40 hours of total gameplay including the main story and optional scenarios.

The story branches into multiple routes, with each route expected to take approximately **12–17 hours** to complete.

*Estimated without using auto-battle, speed-up, or skip functions.*

Depending on the path you choose, the nations explored in the story, the meaning behind certain maps, the positions of your allies, and ultimately the ending itself will change.

In addition to the main story, the game features optional scenarios and flashback events told from the perspectives of individual characters, adding an ensemble-drama element to the narrative.

There is no permanent character death, but defeated units may suffer injury penalties.

Rather than permanently losing a character, the consequences of battle remain with your army in other ways, aiming to preserve tactical tension without sacrificing accessibility.

*Verdant Requiem* is not a conventional fantasy story built around a simple conflict between good and evil.

Instead, it tells a war chronicle shaped by competing ideals, political schemes, and the circumstances of three nations.

At the heart of the story lies the balance between those three powers.

One nation is blessed with abundant resources.

Another is shaped by faith.

A third thrives through trade and scholarship.

None of their circumstances are simple, and even those who stand against you have reasons they cannot abandon.

The main story primarily follows Leonis, but optional scenarios and flashback events also place the spotlight on his companions and people from across the three nations.

To avoid spreading characterization too thin, the number of playable allies is intentionally somewhat smaller than in many traditional SRPGs.

In return, the game places greater emphasis on each character's background, position within the world, relationships, and personal story.

Support conversations also feature character voice acting.

Classic Tactical SRPG Combat

Combat in *Verdant Requiem* is built around the fundamentals of classic tactical RPGs.

In addition to familiar mechanics such as the weapon triangle, critical hits, effective damage, and skills, the game features a **flanking follow-up system** based on unit positioning, as well as **Combat Arts** that emphasize the individual strengths of each character.

Victory is not simply about defeating enemies.

Where you position your units, who initiates an attack, and when you choose to use a Combat Art can all change the course of battle.

Every move matters.

The goal is to deliver the kind of deliberate, position-focused tactical gameplay that defines the SRPG genre.

A Strong Focus on Presentation

Considerable effort has also gone into presentation, with the goal of making both the story and battles feel more memorable.

Combat features character cut-ins and dedicated Combat Art effects, while event scenes make use of weather, fog, lighting, camera effects, and other visual techniques to establish the atmosphere of each scene.

The game also incorporates simulated bloom, water reflections, noise effects, and other visual processing techniques.

Although *Verdant Requiem* is developed in SRPG Studio, extensive work has gone into creating a visual identity that goes beyond the engine's default appearance.

Character portraits blink, map sprites feature additional animations, and both modified and original pixel art assets are used throughout the game.

The UI in particular includes custom visual processing intended to connect the game's presentation with one of its central themes: **balance**.

The aim is to create an experience in which the systems, presentation, and world itself feel connected.

Unique Systems

In addition to standard tactical maps, *Verdant Requiem* features several original systems focused on managing and maintaining your army.

Two of the most important are:

**Military Logistics**

Manage three key resources: **Salt, Food, and Minerals**.

**Alignment Balance**

Leonis' alignment changes according to the player's actions, influencing both his abilities and the strength of the army as a whole.

Other facilities and systems also support your forces outside of battle, including a **Mobile Canteen** and **Arcane Mineral Research Laboratory**.

Winning battles is only one part of leading an army.

You must also decide how to use limited supplies, how to sustain your forces, and what direction your army should ultimately take.

Those decisions form an important part of the game.

In addition, the game features over **40,000 Japanese characters of Support Conversations**, with character voice acting included.

The **Tea Time** interaction system is unvoiced, but contains more than **50,000 Japanese characters of dialogue**. Presented from the player's point of view, it allows you to spend time with individual characters and talk with them about a wide variety of topics.

Through these conversations, you can discover more about each character's personality, values, relationships, and even sides of them that may never appear on the battlefield.

A Heavier Tactical Experience with Resource Management

*Verdant Requiem* is not designed as a simple SRPG in which you move directly from one battle map to the next.

The Military Logistics system revolves around three resources:

・Salt

・Food

・Minerals

These resources are not only part of the army's logistical needs, but can also be used through various base facilities and systems.

Leonis' alignment also changes according to the player's actions.

These changes affect Leonis himself, allied units, and the army as a whole—and can even influence major branches in the story.

For this reason, players looking for a light and straightforward SRPG may find the game heavier than expected.

On the other hand, players who enjoy taking their time with **story, tactics, army management, and resource management** may find the experience especially rewarding.

# Recommended For Players Who Enjoy:

- Tactical RPGs / SRPGs

- Story-driven games and military fantasy

- Political intrigue and conflicts between competing ideals

- Following character backgrounds and relationships in depth

- Classic tactical RPG combat

- Resource management and military logistics

- SRPG Studio games with extensive custom visuals, presentation, and systems

The choices you make will affect not only the journey of Leonis and his companions, but the future of the entire continent.

Will you preserve the balance?

Or will you break it?

Your choices will determine the fate of this land.

【Demo Save Data Transfer】

Please note that transferred demo data is not officially supported for certain features, such as achievements. If you would still like to carry over your save data, please follow the instructions in the image below.

【Playthroughs and Clear Points (CP)】

New Game Cycles and Clear Points (CP)

- The game features **three story routes**.

- The route branch occurs in **Chapter 10**.

- Clearing each route awards **Clear Points (CP)**.

CP rewards are as follows:

- Clearing the **Empire Route**: 10 CP

- Clearing the **Holy Nation Route**: 10 CP

- Clearing the **Third Route**: 20 CP

CP can be used when selecting **New Game** to exchange for bonus items.

Once CP has been awarded, spent points are restored the next time you begin a new game.

For example:

10 CP owned → 6 CP spent → Start another New Game → CP returns to 10.

Please note that after clearing the Third Route and obtaining 20 CP, viewing the ending of either the Empire Route or Holy Nation Route will cause the stored CP value to return to 10.

Viewing the Third Route ending again will restore it to 20.

For this reason, we recommend keeping a save file from **Chapter 25 immediately before clearing the Third Route**.

Back up

Please refer to the instructions below regarding backups.

Important Notes

- This game was created with the assistance of AI tools. Please refer to the relevant disclosure and rating information for details.

- DLC shown or referenced within the game is **not included with the Steam version** and must be purchased separately. Please refer to the Steam community board for details.

- This game uses plugins that are currently **not compatible with Steam Deck**.

Streaming and Other Activities

Streaming, gameplay videos, monetized videos, archived streams, clips, and similar content are permitted.

Please observe the following guidelines:

- For major story spoilers, please consider warning viewers in the title or description.

- Harassment or abusive content directed at viewers, the game, or anyone involved in its development is prohibited.

- Content must comply with generally accepted standards of public decency.

- If possible, we would appreciate it if you let the developer know when you create or stream content featuring the game.

a quiet place to grow

Verdreamia is a gardening game with no fail states, no timers, and nothing to defend while away, only tend when you're there. Neglect a dream for a month and it waits for you, a little sleepy.

plant a dream anywhere

Twelve places to begin: rolling meadow, mountain meadow, verdant field, river valley, mystic dune, tropical shore, raised beds, greenhouse, a Victorian conservatory, a great room, a blank canvas, and a garden of pods drifting past a window of stars. Forty plus species, from daisies and foxgloves to moonbells that only glow after dark.

every plant is grown, not placed

Plants are not prefab. Each specimen is generated from a seed and its own history of care, so no two are alike and yours regrow exactly as they were on any machine, forever.

paint what you love

Frame any view and it becomes a painting on your gallery wall. That gallery is the room you return to, and the record of what your gardens looked like on the days you loved them most. Eight art styles restyle a whole dream at once, from impressionism to old masters.

Every dream grows in one of two worlds, and you can move it between them whenever you like. Golden hush grows soft, rounded shapes in long honey light, and its blooms glow like small lanterns as the day fades. Classic is the uncanny garden of our dreams. Each art style can be applied to enhance the gallery framing of your dream.

the journal remembers

Quiet joys instead of quests. Press a flourishing bloom to keep its cultivar, and the journal fills with what you noticed rather than what you completed. Send a postcard of a painting to a friend; the whole dream travels inside the picture, and they can walk through it.

and it is always the right time

Generative music with its own feel. Rain on greenhouse panes. A sun you can pin where you like it.

Forge turrets at the anvil, chase impossibly rare rolls and hold the wall against endless monsters in an incremental idle tower defense.

Strike the anvil. Pray for Eternal.

Every forge rolls a new turret, and every turret has a rarity: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Exotic, Mythic, Ancient, Divine, Celestial... and Eternal. The rarer the roll, the bigger the anvil charge, the louder the reveal and the harder that turret hits. Level up your forge to tilt the odds, then forge ten at once.

Very, very rare loot

Mutated turrets come out of the forge with a mutagen on top: Ember, Frost, Tremor, Midas and more. Enemies burst into coins, gems and ingots, and rare drops shower the wall. One lucky strike can change your whole defense.

Build your defense

17 turrets, each with its own way to fight: Tesla chains, Cryo Lance freezes, Venom poisons, Shredder bleeds, Mortar shells from afar, Lullaby puts the horde to sleep. Place them on your wall, socket glyphs into their slots, equip relics and grow your castle through its skill tree.

Hold the wall

Waves of armored brutes, menders, splitters and phantoms march on your castle across five regions, from the Ember Yard to the Obsidian Spire. Each region ends with a boss: the Forge Warden, the Iron Marshal, the Glacial Warden, the Cinder Titan and the Obsidian Sovereign.

Progress that stays

Nothing resets. Every turret, glyph, relic and castle upgrade is yours to keep. Speed the battle up to 5x and watch it run, or step in with castle powers and boosters when the horde gets thick.

Features

  • 17 turrets in 11 rarities, from Common to Eternal

  • Rare mutated turrets with 11 mutagens

  • Forge levels that tilt the odds, plus x10 forging

  • 8 glyphs to socket into your turret slots

  • 24 relics: active strikes and passive blessings

  • A 54-node castle skill tree and castle powers

  • Burn, poison, freeze, bleed, stun and sleep

  • 14 enemy types and 5 bosses across 5 regions and 78 stages

  • Quests with rewards and boosters that drop mid-battle

  • Idle-friendly: 1x, 2x and 5x battle speed, permanent progression

  • Pixel art turrets, monsters and bosses

You are a doom metal band. The venue is Hell. Twenty-seven gigs stand between you and getting off this stage — three fights per circle, nine circles deep, with a boss waiting at the end of each one.

VESTIBULE is a roguelike deckbuilder about building a band, stacking riffs, and hitting hard enough to kill things that are already dead.

Every fight gives you a set number of Strikes to work with — four, most runs. Between them you play cards: riffs that buff your members, utility that keeps you alive, embers that pay for all of it.

Then you Strike, and every member swings at once — one multiplier cascade of cards, Riff Chains, artifacts and pedals, all stacking into a single number.

Eighteen musicians across nine roles — guitarists, a drummer, a synth player, a vocalist, and a few things that aren't technically people. Ten keywords define how they play, and they stack: FRENZIED, BLASTBEAT, DISSONANCE, DIRGE, ANCHOR, TRICKSTER, and more.

Only the third fight of each circle — the boss — has a real trick up its sleeve. The Drifter survives its own death, once. The Devourer heals off every card you play. Lucifer gets two full health bars.

Certain cards, played back to back in the same Strike, chain into each other for a real multiplier spike. The chains aren't listed anywhere in the UI — you find them by playing. (There's a toggle if you'd rather just be told.)

Nine circles, Dante's own, three fights each: Limbo, Lust, Gluttony, Greed, Anger, Heresy, Violence, Fraud, Treachery. Then Lucifer — two phases, 6,660 HP — waiting at the bottom. About one run in a hundred sees him dead. He's meant to be a wall.

Between fights: a shop, a descent choice, and if you've got the Stash for it, something from the Dealer — a gamble on a one-fight buff that can just as easily go bad.

Five starter decks, each a different way to play: Standard is balanced and chain-dense, the Shredder is pure aggro, the Chaos deck reshuffles itself at random every single run, the Engineer builds around card copies, and the Survivor gives every member a second chance before they go down. Beat one, unlock the next.

Climb the Stakes and the whole thing gets meaner — more enemy damage, less healing between fights, the Dealer charging more — until Demonic drops you to three Strikes a fight instead of four.

  • BRONZE — baseline, full heal between fights. ×1.0 score

  • SILVER — enemies +2 damage. ×1.5 score

  • GOLD — enemies +2 damage, +6% HP. ×2.0 score

  • OBSIDIAN — +3 damage, +12% HP. Half healing. Dealer +50%. ×2.5 score

  • BLOOD — +4 damage, +19% HP. No healing at all. ×3.0 score

  • DEMONIC — three Strikes, not four. +6 damage. No healing. ×4.0 score

The soundtrack is doom metal, recorded rather than assembled. Real riffs, written for the circle you're standing in.

LAUNCHING OCTOBER 2026. Vestibule is in active development. Everything above — the band, the decks, all nine circles, Lucifer — is built and running. What's left before launch is balance, polish, and whatever more playtesting turns up.

Veyrasol is a real-time massively multiplayer strategy game set across the stars of the Veyra Spiral galaxy. Build and expand your colonies, manage production chains, and assemble powerful fleets to explore, defend, and conquer.

Choose your path by joining one of three factions:

- Vanguard - masters of offense and aggressive expansion

- Aegis - defensive specialists who fortify and outlast

- Concord - diplomats who thrive on alliances and negotiation

Team up with other commanders in alliances, coordinate strategy through in-game chat, and battle for territory in seasons that reset roughly every 120 days, giving every player a fair shot at the top of the leaderboard.

KEY FEATURES

- Real-time colony building and resource management

- Fleet command and tactical combat

- Three distinct factions with unique playstyles

- Alliance diplomacy and large-scale warfare

- Recurring ~120-day seasons for fresh competitive play

- Cross-platform: play on web and Steam — mobile coming at launch

Veyrasol is free to play and currently in active development. Join now and help shape a growing community of commanders inspired by the golden age of browser strategy games.

In the arena, cards alone won't win. You must conquer the battlefield too.

Virtus Arenae is a tactical card game where every creature you summon steps onto the battlefield. Place it, move it, sacrifice it: on a 5×5 board, a single tile can decide the match.

Four tribes. Four ways to win.

The Divine: guardians, angels and other celestial beings. Their light cleanses afflictions, heals wounds and shields their allies. Every sanctified tile becomes a fortress.

The Infernal: demons and devils set the arena ablaze, burn their foes turn after turn and turn the board into an inferno where only they thrive.

The Darkness: specters and monstrous creatures wield terrifying spells to paralyze, haunt and disrupt their enemies. Whoever controls fear controls the game.

The Sylvan: mighty beasts, elves and ancients spread their forest tile by tile until it covers the arena. Driven by nature itself, they are fearsome opponents.

The board is your weapon

Cover the arena in flames, forests, darkness or holy light, raise walls, open portals. Every floor favors one tribe and punishes others. Fight over Evolution Badges that make your creatures stronger, and break through to the enemy line to strike your opponent.

Forge your legend

Earn cards by playing, build your deck and sharpen your strategy against a relentless AI, then test your skills against other players (online PvP coming soon).

Features

  • A tactical card game on a board: movement, positioning and terrain matter as much as your cards
  • 4 playable tribes with radically different playstyles
  • Floors that reshape the arena every turn
  • Unique abilities: flying creatures, rebirth, summoning, lifesteal, riposte…
  • Card collecting and deckbuilding
  • Single-player mode against the AI, online PvP coming soon


Key art: Julien Motteler

A young king sits the throne of Tasvirate. The court bows to him — but it listens to you.

As his Vizier, you do not rule. You advise. Every petition, every plot, every war begins as a few quiet words in the king's ear — and becomes your legacy, or your ruin.

The power is his. The words are yours.

Each turn brings a decision: a desperate petitioner, a scheming noble, a province in revolt. You choose the counsel — but the king has a mind of his own. His temper, his fears, and his trust in you decide whether your advice becomes law or is thrown back in your face. Win him, steer him, or be undone by him.

A court that remembers

  • Factions watch every move and shift their loyalty as you favor or betray them.

  • A realm to hold together — treasury, provinces, and an uneasy peace between rival houses.

  • A reputation that follows you: schemer, reformer, butcher, saint.

  • Rivals, lovers, protégés, and a spouse whose fates twist around your own.

Intrigue has a long memory

  • Conspiracies brew across many turns — smother a coup before it reaches the throne, or quietly ride it to power.

  • Wars, assassinations, and succession crises play out as slow-burning arcs that end in triumph or catastrophe.

  • The court hides as much as it reveals. You act on what you can learn — never on everything you wish you knew.

Every service ends — how is up to you

Retire with honour, to a house full of the court's gifts. See the boy you counselled become a king who needs no counsel. Or be dismissed in disgrace, cut down in a coup, met by a knife in the dark. The court is fair: what comes back to you is what you did — the debts you forgave, the truths you kept from the king, the people you passed over. And then a new service begins at another court: a king of a different nature, a new rival, new neighbours.

Features

  • A turn-based story of court intrigue where no two reigns are alike.

  • Create your Vizier and decide how you'll serve — or how you'll rise.

  • A living court of factions, rivals, and relationships that react to every choice.

  • A king you learn to read: five natures, and each weighs the same advice differently.

  • A rival with a face: designs of their own, letters between seasons, and a last throw you answer in three exchanges.

  • Evenings in the hall: nard against a king who plays as he rules, liar's dice with the court, and six quiet tables — from the mosaic to the astrolabe.

    Branching arcs and many ways for a reign — and a life — to end.

  • Fully playable in 7 languages: English, Russian, German, Spanish, French, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil).

  • 42 achievements, painterly portraits, cinematic openings, and a score made for the game.

The power is the king's. The reign is yours to shape — or to lose.

No story, no dialogue - Void Descent is only here to offer pure bullet heaven action.

Take control of your ship and destroy everything that comes at you. Weapons fire automatically so you can focus entirely on movement, positioning, and survival using mouse, keyboard, or controller.

Explore over 80 billion loadout combinations.

Customize your weapon loadout with 5 distinct elemental types. Boost each element's effectiveness with dedicated Mastery Upgrades, then amplify your power even further with Elemental Synergies combining two elements to unleash devastating fusion effects and unique abilities.

Playing it safe isn't an option here. Void Descent forces you on the offensive with a real-time Combat Rank system.

Stay aggressive, weave through swarms, and thread the needle through enemy fire to push your rank to the limit. Fall back or take hits, and your rank tanks fast. The higher your Combat Rank, the more massive your score multiplier grows.

Slow down time whenever you want with Time Dilation because why restrict something this fun with a cooldown?

Releasing your controls instantly drops time to 10% speed. Evaluate the swarm, line up your next move, soak in the weapon effects, or answer the colleague who just called your name on a work call. When you're ready, start steering again to smoothly ramp back to full speed and plunge straight into the chaos.

Void Descent offers 2 completely different graphics modes.

Retro 2D offers that classic vector arcade feel with maximum visual clarity while saving battery when playing on handhelds. Modern 3D showcases high-fidelity space combat, detailed ship models, and rich lighting when you have graphical horsepower to spare.

Enter the Augment Lab to unlock game-changing offensive, defensive, and utility perks.

Use resources harvested from Titans and Nexus Prime to unlock augments and construct absurd synergies to tackle Ascension tiers and push deep into Endless Mode.

Just you, your loadout, and the will to live.

After conquering all 5 Ascension tiers, unlock the endless Void Descent Mode. Equip up to 3 augments, adapt to randomized debuffs every 10 waves, and battle escalating Titans every two minutes. Reach periodic checkpoints to cleanse debuffs, repair your hull, or stack even more augments to create a truly broken build. How long can you survive?

Void Descent is a solo passion project built for fans of high-octane action roguelikes. A huge thank you to everyone who has played the demo and shared feedback so far. I'm actively building and tuning this game based on what you think. I hope you enjoy!

Void Forge

A pixel-art auto-chess game centered on automated combat.

🩸 Core Gameplay: Strategy Before Battle

No micro-management, no APM test. Your battlefield is decided before the fight begins—

Recruit champions from wandering swordsmen, elemental mages, void creatures, and crimson cultists

Equip them with Relics that rewrite skill mechanics and tactical roles

Deploy them on the board, then watch as AI executes your carefully crafted strategy

Every victory is a victory of your strategy.

🌍 World: An Epic Forged in Blood

Your champions do not appear from nowhere. Behind them stand—

The blood-soaked empire of the Crimson Tyrant, whose only law demands tribute in blood

The secretive mages of the Elemental Conclave, seeking balance between ice and fire

The stasis sentinels of the Void Cult, gazing into reality from fissures in the abyss

The last knights of the Glory Court, holding fast to a faith long since fallen among ruins

Their grudges, hatreds, and fates will intertwine and play out across your arena.

🎮 Game Features

Auto-chess combat, strategy reigns supreme: Deploy before battle, watch the outcome unfold

A wide roster of champions: Each character has unique mechanics and backstory

Relic crafting: Multiple synergies that modify skill mechanics, not just stack numbers

Progressive difficulty: Normal → Elite → Boss, every monster hides an advanced rule set

Pixel aesthetics: Retro pixel art with sharp, fluid action sprite animations

No gacha: All champions can be unlocked through in-game progression

📖 Each chapter tells its own story

After the Heart of the Kalidor World shattered, on the night the Crimson Moon rose, the last emperor of Kalidor drank the primordial blood of a foreign god.

From that moment, the land was covered by the Blood Law, and kingdoms turned into prisons of blood. Elemental beings and void creations emerged one after another.

You stand at the convergence point of these fractured worlds. You will become the Gatherer, crossing the abyss to bring lost heroes back to camp, delving deeper into the truth behind the world's shattering.

Wishlist now and witness the end of the story.

Void Inc. is a surreal management sim with hands-on IT tasks, corporate nonsense, and creeping horror. As a startup's Head of Technology, you'll manage the team, tackle your own workload, and answer to the CEO while the office gets stranger around you.

A relaxing desk job. Allegedly.

Manage a Company

Plan company work, decide priorities and balance growth and stability within the company

Upgrade and Hire your way to Success

Upgrade your office, get better coffee and more reliable servers. Hire and fire staff to help manage the ever-increasing workload.

Play Mini-Games or Delegate them to your staff

Each pillar (infrastructure, customer trust, code and databases) has their own unique puzzle game, play them yourself, or delegate them to your team.

Keep the Company Healthy

Balance the four pillars and Void Inc and keep the customers happy, the lights on, and the CEO off your back.

Discover the Truth

As your sanity slowly slips, you investigate the cracks in the shell of Void Inc. What is the company hiding, and what are they really doing here?

Face an onslaught of endless enemy squadrons and survive hostile space in Void Strike. Create dynamic builds from a wide range of weapons, cursed upgrades, pilot abilities, spaceships, and synergies in order to survive wave after wave.

Are you skilled enough to shatter the fleet, or will the void tear your tiny fighter apart?

Build a War Machine Every Run

Flood the screen with bullets, split formations with railguns, drag enemies into gravity wells, chain lightning through clustered ships, burn them inside solar auras, or let auto turrets and seeker pods hunt while you focus on dodging. How you fight them is your choice alone.

Unlock Pilots, Airframes, and Synergies

Take control of a growing roster of pilots and pair them with unlockable ships. With their different strengths and playstyles, they make each run feel different from the last.

Send Your Pilot Roaming

The game never stops. Send your pilot on roaming expeditions to collect resources, uncover rewards, and strengthen your next run through a lighter idle side mode.

Survive Escalating Waves and Colossal Bosses

The longer you last, the worse the space gets. Enemy formations grow denser, special threats enter the battle, and massive bosses arrive to test you.

Earn, Upgrade, Repeat

Every mission earns credits, unlocks, and new ways to make your next run stronger

Features

  • 1-bit arcade dogfighting mixed with survival roguelite progression

  •  Hands-on action or idle mode

  • Dozens of weapons, upgrades, cursed choices, and synergies

  • Multiple pilots with unique skill trees and abilities

  • Unlockable airframes with distinct playstyles

  • Boss fights against massive experimental war machines

  • Permanent progression, credits, salvage, challenges, and unlocks

  • Solo play, local co-op, and peer-to-peer multiplayer

  • Keyboard, controller, mouse, and touchscreen support

A Love Letter to the Golden Era

Step into a beautifully crafted overhead 2D realm that evokes the nostalgia, depth, and wonder of classic 16-bit RPGs in full uncompressed 32bit color fidelity across 33,000 individual animation frames and a 13 palette weather VFX taxonomy that mirrors the elemental damage you take, building a unique anima / aura based system that defines your character from the types of damage you take. Built with a passion for tactical challenge and rich storytelling, Void Walkers X64 merges timeless retro mechanics with modern progression depth.

Your aura fights their aura.

A 70-hour classic JRPG where every boss is fought twice — once for their health, once for their soul. 183 maps, 40 hubs, five paths to ten classes. Runs on the PC you already own.

Reality is coming apart

Realms are being drawn inward toward a point of absolute erasure. The Void Shogun — a tyrant born from the dark between dimensions — is accelerating the collapse, turning every fallen world into another province of his infinite empire.

You are a master monk, pulled through a dimensional tear with nothing but your training. You begin in a conscription camp with no weapon and no allies. You end as a Sovereign — or you break the cycle entirely.

Between those two points: 183 hand-authored maps, 173 quests across twelve branching arcs, 40 hub locations with their own merchants and secrets, and ten full class mastery chains. A world map that keeps opening outward, towns worth talking to everyone in, dungeons that punish sloppiness. Fast menus, snappy transitions, no filler between you and the next fight.

The Anima War

Combat runs in real time on a charge gauge — attack, skill, magic, item, defend, all one keypress deep. Chain hits and your combo climbs, the audio tightens, and skill effects escalate into full-screen bursts.

Then you meet something with an aura, and the floor changes.

There's a second bar beneath the health bar, and it belongs to your soul.

Against elites and bosses, every resonant strike shoves at the enemy's anima field — and they shove back. Overwhelm them and their guard chips away. Match them and you lock, both fields grinding. Lose and you're Suppressed: perks damped, damage spiking, growth halted until you break free.

Crack the guard completely and you trigger an Anima Break — the screen flares, the fight stops, and for a few seconds they take massive bonus damage and cannot cast. Empty everything into that window.

Bosses stop being health sponges you out-level. They become puzzles you solve.

Five paths, ten classes

How you fight defines who you become. Every path starts humble and ends legendary.

What you actually get

183 map areas. 40 Towns / Unique areas with interactive lore, combat arenas, vistas, npc homes, dungeons, and shops.

Places that remember you

Circuit foundries, blizzard forges, fairy caves, a ghost ship, shogun temples, a graveyard that doesn't stay quiet. Each with merchants, amenities, explore nodes and an arena — and NPCs whose disposition shifts with everything you do.

Build your party by beating it

Challenge avatar opponents in any hub's arena. Win, and you recruit them — naming them yourself as they join, each with their own class skills and personal arc.

The world as it became

Soul Hacker Ascension reopens all 40 locations as a Corrupted Suite: the same geography twisted, NPCs inverted, and darker retellings of arcs you already lived — leading to the true ending.

NG+: A ladder, not a lap

Carry your resonance forward through escalating cycles that raise enemy tiers and unlock Echo content — ending in Sovereign mode: permadeath, no shops, maximum difficulty.

5 Tier Aura & Anima System: Resonance progression

Climb from Dormant to Sovereign. Your tier raises damage, opens gated regions, unlocks intimidate and persuade dialogue, and decides whether you can break a boss's guard at all. The elemental damage you take effects your player with the unique anima subsystem.

Reasons to wander

Arena ladders, bounty contracts, hidden caches, lore tablets, secret bosses, artifact hunts, and 24 shops whose stock shifts with your standing.

Runs on what you already have

Three selectable rendering backends — DirectX 11, Vulkan, and a software compose path — so the game runs on a modern GPU or a decade-old laptop. A dedicated Low VRAM mode holds it inside a 128 MB video memory budget for handhelds and low-spec machines, streaming assets on demand. Battle effects are fully procedural, generated per cast rather than loaded from texture sheets.

Turn it off and the engine opens up: higher-resolution atlases, richer effect layers, full-fidelity lighting. Same 70-hour game, tuned to your machine instead of the other way around.

VOID WALKERS X64 · Classic JRPG · Single-player · Early Access November
Features, balance and content subject to change during Early Access.

About the Development

Void Walkers X64 is a passionate solo labor of love, built from the ground up outside of bloated, high-level corporate frameworks. Built entirely by an independent developer utilizing a custom-tailored C++ engine stack (IIRIS Engine), the game bypasses traditional commercial middleware to achieve deterministic precision, zero engine bloat, and authentic low-level optimization.

The Toolchain & Independent R&D

Crafted through a rigorous custom toolchain combining modern efficiency with classic design principles, the production pipeline leans heavily into raw code, bespoke map handling, and custom spatial registries (Atlas Architect & Rig Forge). It is an uncompromising showcase of what a dedicated solo developer can accomplish with modern engineering discipline and a respect for hardware-level efficiency.

Published by Lux Aura

Brought to you by Lux Aura—an independent creative imprint and digital sonic temple—the game's atmosphere is backed by a deeply integrated auditory experience designed to immerse players in its dark fantasy world.

VoltHaven is real-time management simulation of electric grid.

You start from scratch in village without energy infrastructure.

Build various power sources and utility buildings as backbone of your grid. Connect first customers and earn money to expand. Advance from makeshift or cheap & obsolete technology to modern power plants, to be able to connect more customers or cut running costs. You can also engage in growing crops or mining resources to up your cash flow.

And while doing this, try to maintain reliable electricity flow with minimal power outages.

Build anywhere, surroundings will adapt.

Reorganize anything when needed.

Connecting structures to grid makes energy flow.

Refuel and upgrade power plants.

Understand weather impact on renewable sources.

Farm & sell produce to up cashflow.

Features

  • energy generation types like Thermal, Wind, Solar, Nuclear, Hydro

  • electricity sources ranging from small kilowatt generators to high megawatt power plants

  • your customers will be individual households, small businesses and large factories

  • commodities (like Diesel, Coal or Wood) are used mainly for fuel, but you can also produce and trade them

  • adapt to local and seasonal weather changes

  • designed for Free play/Sandbox as base mode, with Campaign and Challenge missions built on it

  • underlying simulation model with real-time calculation of power flow in grid structures

  • uses individual customer's time-based energy profiles

  • renewable power depends on wind speed, sun elevation or temperature, with intraday and seasonal variances

  • weather and economy parameters are based on present European data

About the Game

Voltswarm is a single-player 3D bullet heaven about one small robot facing an ever-growing swarm of industrial machines. Your weapons aim and fire automatically, so survival depends on movement, positioning, threat reading, and the build choices you make under pressure.

Gameplay

Draft a starting weapon, collect XP from destroyed machines, and choose upgrades as the swarm grows denser. Combine up to two auto-firing weapons with stat-changing cores and behavior-changing mods. Collect gold, open tiered chests, visit The Scrapper's temporary shop, and activate optional boss portals when you are ready to raise the stakes.

Features

  • Automatic weapons that keep the focus on movement and positioning
  • 11 industrial-themed weapons with distinct attack patterns and upgrade paths
  • Build-defining cores and mods across five rarity tiers
  • A 3D voxel industrial-toy art style designed to keep large swarms readable
  • Six regular enemy types, elites, and two summonable bosses
  • Chests, XP collection, in-run gold, and The Scrapper's temporary shop
  • A ten-minute survival run with escalating enemy density and optional repeated boss fights
  • Keyboard and gamepad input with remappable controls

VoxMancer is a voice-driven 3D magic action game where spoken words become real in-game spells.

Magic should not feel like choosing from a menu.

Instead of relying only on hotkeys, you speak your spells out loud. Say what you want, shape it with your words, and cast it into battle against other spellcasters.

Want a simple fireball? Say it.

Want it faster, larger, piercing, homing, or completely ridiculous? Try it.

Shout with the same passion you had as a kid, or chant like the legendary spellcasters you grew up watching in fantasy films, anime, and games.

For certain signature spells, the longer and more dramatic the invocation, the more powerful and spectacular the magic becomes.

Cast in the language that feels most natural to you.

Say it. Shape it. Cast it.

Your Voice Is Your Spellbook

Remember shouting made-up attacks with your friends as a kid and wishing they could actually happen?

VoxMancer turns that childhood fantasy into magical combat.

The fun is not only in casting a powerful spell. It is in saying the spell out loud, committing to the ridiculous phrase, and letting everyone hear it happen.

A duel can feel serious one second and completely chaotic the next. One player might deliver the perfect invocation and unleash a devastating attack. Another might panic, say something absurd, and trigger a magical failure that blows up in their face.

Every fight becomes a mix of imagination, timing, pressure, and chaos. You are not simply memorizing a fixed list of abilities. You are deciding what to say in the moment, shaping the spell through language, and dealing with whatever happens next.

Some spells are simple.

Some spells are powerful.

Some spells are ridiculous.

Some spells fail spectacularly.

Your voice is your spellbook.

Your imagination is the weapon.

Key Features

Voice-Driven Spellcasting

Cast magic by speaking naturally. Say the spell you want instead of selecting every ability from a rigid hotbar. Cast in the language that feels most natural to you.

Shape Spells With Your Words

Modify spells through language. Make them faster, larger, piercing, homing, rapid-fire and more.

Dramatic Invocation Casting

Short calls are perfect for fast combat. For certain signature spells, longer and more theatrical invocations can unleash greater magical power and spectacle.

Magical Duels Built Around Speech

Battle other spellcasters in fights where what you say matters—and where everyone can hear the spell you dared to cast.

Imagination-Driven Combat

Combat is not only about reflexes. It is about choosing the right spell idea, saying it under pressure, and watching your words become magic.

Elemental Spell Foundations

Begin with elemental magic, then reshape it through spoken modifiers, combinations, and different styles of casting.

Multilingual Voice Spell Input

VoxMancer is designed to support voice spell input across multiple languages, allowing players to cast using spoken commands in the language they are most comfortable with.

Ultimate Magical Spectacle

Unleash devastating signature attacks, strange surprises, hidden spells, and over-the-top magical outcomes that make battles exciting to play and fun to watch.

Magical Failure Feedback

Not every idea will work exactly the way you expect. When the magic fails, it fails with style.

The game of kings, reimagined for modern warfare.

Voxel Gambit takes the timeless rules of chess and injects them with the strategic depth of a turn-based tactical game. Forget the flat, predictable 2D grid; here you will face battles in full 3D environments, where the terrain, your resources, and the enemy's intelligence change with every match.

From Pieces to Modular Warriors Your units are not just wooden figures or images painted on 2D squares. Pawns and bishops have taken up arms as Monks, Rogues, Clerics, and Rangers. Each piece in your squad features a specific design and stats, with their equipment and armor moving in unison in the heat of battle. Utilize the Effort system and Action Points (AP) to decide whether it's worth risking it all on an attack that pushes beyond your limits or if you should maintain a defensive stance.

Procedural Battlefields You will never play the same match twice. The procedural generation engine creates unique maps tailored to 5 different size scales. Adapt your tactics to the terrain conditions as you march across 4 distinct biomes that boost specific piece types:

  • Meadows: Open fields ideal for bishops to utilize their long-range attacks.

  • Mountains: Rugged terrains that benefit the signature L-shaped movement of the cavalry.

  • Caves: Enclosed, labyrinthine spaces where the pawns' scouting will be crucial.

  • Deserts: Open areas filled with rocks and dead trees that will hinder your path across the battlefield, but where finding a straight line to the enemy will highly benefit pieces acting as rooks.

Multi-Layered Artificial Intelligence You are not facing a traditional chess AI. The enemy analyzes the battlefield using a three-layered tactical behavior system. They will evaluate whether to adopt one stance or another according to the state of the battlefield, while each piece executes expert movements based on its class.

Key Features:

  • Deep Tactical Combat: Classic chess mechanics expanded with directional damage, optional friendly fire, and dynamic attack ranges.

  • Total Tactical Camera: Command your troops from a strategic top-down aerial camera, or zoom into the action to get a free, up-close view of the damage you deal to your enemies.

  • Immersive HUD: Dynamic on-screen dialogues, character portraits, and a clean interface that gives you total control over your squad's stats.

  • Turn-Based Planning: In a single turn, you can completely wipe out your opponent or be left at the mercy of the artificial intelligence.

  • Biome Buffs: Each biome benefits a specific piece type by granting it extended action range—but beware, this also applies to enemy units.

  • Mirrored Units: Carefully plan which units you bring to the battlefield; they will be the exact same ones the AI uses to make your life miserable.

  • Versatile Inputs: Command the battlefield however you feel most comfortable. Voxel Gambit features full support for keyboard-only gameplay, traditional keyboard and mouse setups, and gamepads/joysticks.

Waronomy is a turn-based fantasy conquest game built in the spirit of classic strategy games where the map, the armies, and your decisions matter more than layers of needless complexity.

It keeps the proven appeal of old-school fantasy conquest: explore the world, raise armies, capture castles, recruit heroes, search ancient ruins, uncover powerful artifacts, and gradually turn a fragile foothold into a dominant empire.

Waronomy is deliberately simple to understand, but difficult to master. There are no bloated systems fighting for your attention, no awkward surprises, and no attempts to over-complicate a formula that already works. Instead, the focus is on clean strategic play: reading the map, choosing your battles, controlling key positions, and making every turn count.

There are many modern improvements, which sit quietly around the experience rather than getting in the way. Faster flow, clearer controls, smoother army management, better feedback, and a more comfortable interface help the game feel fresh while preserving the direct, satisfying nature of classic turn-based conquest.

Your roster. Your show. Your champions.

Run a wrestling promotion in WBS26 Wrestling Booker Simulator. Choose a real-world promotion featured in the game or create your own company, then build a roster and book its future. Decide who headlines, who carries the championships and who gets the next chance to become a star.

Book your show, match by match

Build weekly shows and major events from matches and promos. Choose each match’s participants, rules, length, winner and finish, then arrange the running order and main event. Use the booking forecast to weigh expected quality against the time, risk and cost of your card.

Watch your matches in 3D

Follow your booked matches in 3D broadcasts with entrances, arenas, crowds and championship celebrations. Watch the action, change the playback speed or skip to the result. Your choices in the booking room set the stage for what happens in the ring.

39 real promotions. 750+ real wrestlers and staff.

Scout free agents, negotiate contracts and decide where your talent budget goes. Sign a headliner, develop prospects through your academy or give an overlooked wrestler a place on the card. Build around singles wrestlers, tag teams and factions as your promotion grows.

See the results. Plan the next show.

Review match ratings, the overall show report, attendance and finances. Check changes in wrestler popularity and morale, then use what you learn to plan the next card. Winning a match, pleasing the crowd and making a profit are different parts of running a promotion.

Build rivalries and title histories

Develop rivalries through matches, promos, teams and factions. Use turns, betrayals and interference to change a feud’s direction. Build challengers, track championship reigns and defences, and choose the moment to crown someone new.

Run the business behind the curtain

Choose venues, set ticket prices, hire staff and negotiate sponsorship and broadcast deals. Balance the books while keeping track of owner objectives, locker-room morale and relationships. Promises, opportunities and booking decisions leave a history that can shape future conversations with your wrestlers.

Real-world promotions

WBS26 features 39 real-world wrestling promotions:

Names, logos, trademarks and related materials remain the property of the respective promotions and rights holders.

Try the WBS26 demo and book your first show.

Break their morale. Push the line. Choose your moment.

WHEN ARMIES WAVER is a real-time medieval battle roguelite where you command an entire army, not individual soldiers. Hold against a charge, fall back to regroup, then advance when enemy morale begins to waver. Read the battle line and create your opening.

Push, hold, or fall back

Switch between Advance, Defend, and Retreat while watching morale on both sides and the position of the front line. Commit to an All-Out Charge, or save your orders and stratagems for a better opening. The timing of your commands changes the struggle for ground.

Build a different army with every victory

Choose one of three reward cards after battle. Combine the troops, formations, orders, stratagems, and doctrines you acquire, then prepare your army for its next fight.

  • Shape your strengths with front- and rear-line troops and a formation.
  • Choose when to use charge and defense orders, arrow volleys, and smoke screens.
  • Use passive doctrines to support breakthrough power, endurance, or morale.

Survive the campaign, not just the battle

Choose a path through battles, elite enemies, supplies, rewards, and events. Scout ahead to learn what awaits, then decide whether to take a dangerous fight or give your army a chance to recover.

Reserves replace your losses, but they will not last forever. Spend your strength on the next victory, or preserve it for the final battle. Choose rewards, rebuild your army, and break through the enemy's last defensive line.

WHO THE HELL OPENED THE PORTAL?! is a funny pixel art strategy roguelite where you play as the prince of a good guys fantasy kingdom. Your lands are scattered across islands connected by magical portals.
Yes, traveling through portals is convenient during the day. But at night, those same portals turn into gateways from Hell — and all sorts of bad guys crawl out!

What to expect:

🏰 Day — building, management, expansion
• Develop mines and gather resources to upgrade your kingdom.
• Level up your castle and support buildings to unlock new bonuses.
• Recruit heroes at the tavern — each with unique skills and quirks.
• Send expeditions through portals to explore new islands.
• Capture more territory: more mines → more income → more everything.
• Complete quests for rewards, boosts, and a bit of glory.

A perfectly normal workday for any prince.

👹 Night — defend yourself!
When the sun sets, portals transform into Hell Gates.
Demons, imps, and all kinds of nasties pour out of them. Your job is to:
• Place heroes on defense.
• Strengthen your castle.
• Survive until dawn… preferably alive.

Key Features

🎯 Strategic and tactical kingdom management
🔄 Roguelite cycle with random events
🌍 Variety of islands and biomes with unique resources and bonuses
⚔️ Heroes with unique abilities and different base attributes
💎 Tons of resources, upgrades, and progression choices
🔮 Pixel art + lighthearted humor and a charming atmosphere

👉 Add the game to your wishlist — and may your portal lead somewhere nice for once!
