Four words. Twelve letters. Every discard counts.

WORJONG is a competitive word game for up to four players.

On your turn, draw a tile and discard a tile.

Your goal is to turn 12 letters into four three-letter words, like BIG, DOG, SKY, and FLY.

Everyone can see your discards.

A rival can use one to complete their words, and then you pay for their score.

Clever combos, bigger scores

Points come from scoring conditions, such as turning your four words into a grammatical sentence (YOU ARE BIG NOW) or using no vowels at all (SKY, FLY, GYM, CRY).

The rarer the combination, the bigger the score, and bonus letters add even more.

Keep a finished word, or break it up to chase something bigger?

Every score opens a comeback

When someone scores, only they start from scratch.

Everyone else keeps their words in progress and can strike back right away.

A new bonus letter is also chosen: stick with your words, or rebuild around it?

Features

1. Hints show which letters to let go, so even beginners can play from their very first game

2. Collect every word, grammar pattern, and scoring condition you've scored with, and aim for 100%

3. Solo Battle against the CPU, plus online battles with friends or other players

Full Rules

Learn every rule step by step in the game's Rules section, or through the website link on this page.

Online Multiplayer for 1–4 Players

Play against friends or get matched with other players online.

Just share a room code to play with anyone.

Single-Player Story Mode

Take Tanuki Village back from the humans!

You have 7 days! Collect the land deeds!

In Story Mode, learn tanuki jutsu and cheat by setting off explosions or stopping time!

Story: KEN

Illustrations: KEN

Music: KEN

Voice Cast: Monyai, Asumi Kana

Streaming Guidelines

Streaming and monetization are both permitted.

No prior permission is required.

You may include the game title or Steam store URL, but you do not have to.

WORKS: Motorsport Factory is a top-down tycoon sim about everything that happens before a racing car reaches the circuit.

Manage a motorsport team from the ground up: staff, facilities, car design and development while trying to stay competitive on a limited budget. Secure sponsors, hire mechanics, source parts and keep the operation running long enough to make it to race day.

Five tiers of motorsport stand between your workshop and the being the most prestigious team in motorsport. Progress is not a straight climb - it’s a long-term struggle of financial pressure, technical setbacks and outperforming better-funded rivals.

You manage the operation that makes the racing possible.

Build the car. Prepare the spares. Manage the crew. Get the right driver in the seat. Load the truck. Get everything out of the factory and to the circuit before the departure deadline.

While you wait at the factory the racing happens, watch the timing screens and wait. 

When the results come in your work begins again worn parts, crash damage and everything you learned about the car.

Your crew goes to work. Deliveries arrive. Builders get back to work on the new section of the garage. 

Every job takes time. Every job needs someone to do it.

Where you put things, who you hire, how your workshop is laid out and what your crew is doing right now all matter. The factory isn't a menu. It's a working place.

Each part has a story. Each part has a lifespan. A brand new part at race one is not the same at the end of a season. 

Performance drops off, wear accumulates and eventually a part will fail. Run it too hard and repair it too much and it won't perform the same again. 

You can design parts for performance, endurance or reliability but getting the right balance to cover all three can be impossible

Every part has a breaking point. Every part has a finite mileage lifespan. Every part has a performance drop-off that only reveals itself under real conditions.

The better your facilities and the stronger your technical staff, the more of the truth you can uncover. And in a sport where tenths of a second matter, knowledge is often more valuable than raw performance.

Five tiers of racing with many routes to reach the top. Whether it's from Karting to Open Wheel or Banger racing to Touring Cars, you're picking the route.

Getting into the next series isn't just about winning.

Drivers have careers of their own. Rivals develop. Sponsors can be offended. Contracts have teeth. Regulations change. Last year's dominance can become deemed illegal next season.

You might have the fastest car and no money to run it.

You might have the best driver and nothing worth putting them in.

You might spend an entire season fighting for the last championship point that keeps the team alive.

Grow from a workshop into a full constructor with a design studio, machine shop, wind tunnel and crash-test facilities. Design and develop your own cars part by part. 

The costs are high but the rewards come in trophies and expansions

  • The factory is the game, the race is the exam
    build, prepare, staff and transport your team to the race

  • A complete part lifecycle
    scavenge, buy, test, wear, break, design and manufacture.

  • Build your own technology
    develop components in-house, from basic roll-cages and suspension through to chassis, gearboxes and engines

  • Off-screen racing simulation
    every race produces consequences: results, points, prize money, wear and damage.

  • 5 tiers of motorsport, multiple series to choose from
    with multiple paths through a career.

  • Drivers with careers of their own
    recruit, develop, poach and eventually build a youth academy.

  • A real business to keep alive
    sponsors, contracts, loans, expenses and insolvency.

  • A factory you've built from the ground up
    build rooms, road networks, race bays and workshops even a test track.

  • Regulations that change the game
    technology that dominated last season may be obsolete or illegal next season, motorsport chews out teams who don't adapt.

  • Race reports based on a full race simulation
    Parts you race, the contracts you sign, the drivers and mechanics track side all have an impact in your race performance

WORLD'S GONE MAD.

An anarchic zone, inhabited by antisocial killers, disturbed perverts, mutated half-humans, egomaniacal dictators, and some nice people sprinkled in here and there. 

Swap out and perfect all your body parts and organs. Collect the most powerful loadout of guns, knives and swords. Learn martial skills and neuro-manic psychomanipulation. Choose whose will to enforce and whose cause to help, and lay waste to those who stand in your way... assuming they don't put up a bigger fight than you.

Your body is yours to customize, optimize, and strengthen. Arms, legs, vitals, guts - swap it all out! Make the most of androgen, xenogen and synthetic implants to turn yourself into an athletic monster, an unstoppable tank, an unholy sharpshooter, or anything in between.

Choose from a plethora of melee weapons and firearms to forge your ideal playstyle. Slow and methodical hitmen, lightning-fast swordsmen, sledgehammer juggernauts, machine gun powerhouses, and whoever else you can think of - Waderverse has them all.

What else is in store?

Currently, there is only a demo available on Steam, in which you slash, shoot and run through a small course full of training dummies and try to beat your best time. The game itself - a 2D open-world RPG - will take years to fully create. There are many gameplay systems and mechanics missing from the demo - Mania and active and passive abilities, for example - which will be added in a second demo when enemy AI is finished. If you are interested in the game's development, my socials are listed on this page.

Your village is one of several on a small island. None of the others intend to stay small.

You inherit a tavern and nothing else. Everything after it has to be paid for out of what the village already makes, so you start with ale and you trade upward from there.

Every morning your deck deals you a hand and you work out which card belongs at which door. The same card is worth different things in different villages: a flat two coins in a thin town, six in a thick one where you have built its neighbours or filled the place with tradesmen it likes.

Your villagers turn up with names of their own, a trade they lean toward, and a quirk that pays out in some situations and never in others. Fenn of the Long Table is worth two extra ale a night behind the bar and will not survive a serious argument.

Raise your war banner and the whole island knows where to point. A raid comes down to a duel: two champions, best of three rounds, both swinging at the same time. The defender has the ground and knows it, and whoever you send works no post that night, so a raid costs you a day before anyone throws a punch.

Nobody dies here. Beaten fighters are taken, and they do not come back — they work for whoever took them, permanently. Empty a village of its people and the place is yours: the treasury, the stores, and your pick of the cards it spent a season assembling.

Nights resolve on their own, so a season runs at whatever pace the table keeps. Play one alone against the AI villages, or share the island with other stewards.

In short
  • Six establishments, each paid for in the goods you already make
  • A deck that deals and reshuffles every single day, and cards that read the board around them
  • Villagers with their own names, perks, trades and rarity, from labourers to legends
  • Asynchronous raids, armed in daylight and fought at midnight whether you are watching or not
  • Best-of-three duels with home ground, parries and knockouts
  • Permanent capture instead of death, and conquest of whoever runs out of people first

You are an intern

You are an intern. There is a stack of paper and a button that says SIGN. You click it, a few dollars appear, and nobody explains what you signed.

Soon you pay someone else to do the signing and the number moves without you. Everyone knows this part of an idle game. It is not why you are still here in hour two. Eight tiers sit above the intern, ending at a central bank, and each copy costs 1.15 times the last, which is why hour one and hour ten feel like different games.

Hour two

There is a bull. He is the mascot and he is doing better than you. Sunglasses once you cross a million, a cigar at a hundred million, a Rolex at a billion, a crown at a trillion.

Five tickers reprice every four seconds. You are holding a Bitcoin position you keep promising yourself you will close at 90K. You will not. The price wanders between roughly 18K and 133K with pump and dump shocks on top, so the number you wanted was probably three minutes ago.

Then you find the YOLO button. 35% chance it multiplies your cash by eight, 65% chance it takes 30% off the top, fifteen second cooldown. You can do the math. Nobody does.

When the SEC shows up

The suspicion gauge fills as you earn, and much faster if you buy insider tips, which give x10 income for sixty seconds and are obviously, obviously worth it.

Then they raid you, and it becomes a fight. 100 HP each, four moves, honest percentages. Attack hits 90% for 15 to 25, the boring one that works. Charm lands 75%. Lawyers heal 25 at 95%. Bribery is a coin flip for 40 damage and costs 5% of your capital whether it connects or not.

Winner keeps everything. Loser drops 60% of their fortune. Or you reach prestige 5, move to Switzerland, and the SEC cannot reach you at all. I am told this is realistic.

Where it goes

Prestige spends your cash and pays you back in talent points plus a philosophy you keep forever: Wolf, Oracle, Elon, Banker, and they stack. Run that loop ten times and the IPO unlocks, a full reset for $50B, a permanent x10, and a mode called GLOBAL TYCOON.

Downstairs, a casino. Slots, European roulette with 37 sectors, blackjack where the dealer hits 17, six horses paying up to x40. You type your own bet. Sixteen research projects run on a real clock, thirty minutes to six hours, and keep going with the game closed. Nine luxury items (lambo, yacht, jet, island, rocket) change nothing except the view. I built them anyway and they are my favourite part of the game. There is a photo mode. Take him somewhere nice.

About the money

Made by one person in France. Buy it once and it is yours: no ads, no energy timers, no data collection, and it plays fully offline.

No microtransactions. There is a shop, but the only thing in it is bull skins, and you pay for those with money you earned in the game. I had a paid boost pack ready and cut it. A tycoon about greed does not need to reach into your wallet twice.

Six languages, and there is a demo. The Konami code works.

A roguelite siege defense. The horde marches at your wall in lanes, and

anything that reaches it takes health you cannot fully get back.

Spin, place, transmute

Every turn the reel deals you alchemical symbols. You place them on the

table, then transmute: the board resolves and becomes damage. Where you

put them is the whole decision.

The board grows

Symbols react to their neighbours. Fire beside Fire hits harder. A Seed

grows every turn it survives. Leave a symbol alone long enough and it

promotes into a stronger form that was never in your deck. Symbols come

in elemental families and enemies have weaknesses, so the kind of damage

matters as much as the amount.

Relics, Tools and Rituals

Relics change a rule for the rest of the run. Tools have limited charges

and few slots, so you spend them carefully. Rituals pay out when their

condition is met, which means building toward them turns in advance.

Between sieges

A shop with a short stock. A scavenger running a shell game you can walk

away from. A mason who grants a single favour: open a locked cell, move

a symbol, or destroy one.

Between runs

Losing ends the run but not the progress. Essence carries into a tree of

permanent unlocks, so the next attempt starts with something the last

one did not have.

DRIFT. FIGHT. SURVIVE.


A gap in the roadblock. One more crate. Just enough fuel to make the next turn.

WANTED DRIFT is a top-down roguelite car combat game set in an endless neon city. Your weapons fire automatically; you handle the driving. Slide around corners, boost out of trouble, and fight your way free when the police box you in. Stay alive long enough and patrol cars give way to armored units, drones, tanks, and elite enemies.

BUILD YOUR WAY OUT


Every loot crate gives you a choice. Add a weapon, level up a favorite, or improve your car and firepower. Combine turrets, mines, electrical attacks, and more across up to four weapon slots. A good build can clear a path. You still have to drive through it.

BUILD YOUR GARAGE


Keep the coins you collect and spend them in the garage. Start with the Interceptor and its rear-firing turret, then buy the Jammer Van with its EMP pulse or the heavy Bomb Squad with rear mines. Each car has different handling, durability and a starting weapon to build around.

A STRONGER START


Your score adds up separately for each car, unlocking six permanent powerups as you play. Spend coins to buy them and improve each through three ranks. Choose one to bring into your next run, then reach car level 7 to equip two together.

TAKE THE SHORTCUT. LEAVE A MESS.


Cut through a park, squeeze down an alley, or race along the river as the pursuit tears through the city. Smash fences, benches, trees, and street furniture, sending debris into the chase. Pick daylight, neon nights, or a shifting day-and-night cycle.

HOW LONG CAN YOU KEEP GOING?


Watch your health and fuel while the Wanted level climbs. Push for another upgrade, a higher score, or a little more room to breathe. When the run ends, your collected coins and car progress stay with you. Head back to the garage, choose your powerup and try a different build.

  • Arcade driving with drifting and boost
  • Automatic weapon combat and upgrades chosen during each run
  • Three cars with distinct starting weapons, bought with collected coins
  • Car-specific permanent powerups with three upgrade ranks
  • An endless procedural city with traffic and destructible street props
  • Escalating police pursuits, heavy units, and elite enemies
  • Full controller support, Steam achievements, and Steam Cloud

Ice and water whisper deep within the corridors. Legend says the Wanxiang Corridor holds the very essence of the elements—behind every door lie new foes, treasures, and death.

Wanxiang Corridor: Elements is a 2D top-down roguelike action shooter. You step into the boots of an archer, using tap-shots, charged attacks, and enhanced barrages to fight your way through procedurally generated dungeons—room layouts, enemy compositions, and loot change with every single run.

Master the Power of Ice and Water

Switch between Water and Ice elements freely with a right-click. Soak your enemies in water, then freeze them solid with ice—seize control of the battlefield and craft your own devastating combos.

Forge Your Unique Build

Clear each room and choose one of three upgrades: stats, elemental skills, or survival bonuses. Layer them run after run to create a playstyle that's entirely your own. Every choice reshapes how you fight in the next encounter.

A Dungeon That Never Repeats

Rooms and corridors are generated on the fly by algorithms, with treasure rooms, elite encounters, and boss arenas escalating as you push deeper. From the charging Boar King, to the Frost Cannon beneath the star-lit night, to the Shaman King in the whispering depths, and finally the dreaded Devil Snare that lurks at dawn's edge—each chapter brings a distinct new boss to test your mettle.

Easy to Pick Up, Hard to Put Down

Progressive tutorials, bilingual support (English & Chinese), and gold-based revives after death keep each run tight and satisfying. Jump in anytime—death is never the end.

The Wanxiang Corridor is now fully open. Take up your bow, and may every death bring you one step closer to the truth.

We Want to Hear From You

If you run into any issues or have suggestions for improvement, feel free to reach out through the contact info and community links on the sidebar of this store page.

Wishlist Wanxiang Corridor: Elements now and embark on your elemental journey!

War in Asia is a grand strategy game built around systemic simulation. Its goal is to deeply and comprehensively simulate the East Asian theater of World War II from 1937 to 1945 through three major pillars: military operations, economy, and logistics networks.

Command and Campaigns

War in Asia features its own distinctive wargame-style operational system. Chinese forces are represented primarily at the division level, while Japanese forces are represented primarily at the regiment level, with formations composed down to regiments and battalions.

Through the chain-of-command system, you will take control of the entire Chinese front, appoint your commanders, and organize large-scale campaigns. Campaigns are dynamic operations that unfold over days or even weeks. Every breakthrough and delay along the front can reshape the wider strategic situation.

A unit’s combat effectiveness depends heavily on its condition. Disrupted supply lines, or reckless prolonged high-intensity operations, can rapidly weaken or even collapse your forces.

Units do not appear out of thin air. You may organize new formations based on historical orders of battle or custom formation templates. At the same time, each nation’s industrial and equipment capacity will limit what kinds of formations are realistically viable. Train and equip new units in any region, and assign them the designations you prefer.

Map and Cities

Thanks to a script-driven map editor, War in Asia features more than 300,000 tiles. On one of the most faithful strategic maps of East Asia, you will be able to command all of your forces.

As in the real East Asian theater of World War II, major cities and transportation lines form the core of the game map. Seize and suppress key strategic and resource nodes to secure victory in the war.

Economy and Production

Resources in the game have sources, processing chains, and distribution paths. You must manage your resources by producing basic materials through city buildings, transporting them through the transportation network, and processing them into weapons and equipment that can be delivered to the front.

The transportation network is a vital part of the game. Goods can only be moved between cities through the transportation network you build and control.

Logistics and Transportation

Your frontline capabilities depend on sustained supply. You may decide to concentrate resources in Wuhan to support the Central China front. This may increase local industrial output, but it could also create shortages in other regions.

You may choose to launch an offensive, but if your supply preparations are insufficient, the operation may stall on its own during the advance.

Each military unit receives supplies from a designated city. When that city’s stockpiles are depleted, or when the roads connecting the unit to its supply source are cut, the unit will no longer be able to properly replenish personnel or recover its condition.

Politics and Organization

The game features a unique character system. Assign your characters as frontline commanders or bureaucrats within the government, and allocate tasks according to their different talents.

Characters are an important element in keeping your nation running. Choosing the right people for the right positions can bring major advantages.

International Diplomacy

World War II was a global conflict. As a result, the international situation and changes in other countries’ attitudes toward you will directly affect the battlefield.

Poor diplomacy will create more difficulties for you, while a strong international image can bring meaningful benefits.

You can engage in a wide range of international interactions, leading to different outcomes.

WARCHAIC

Build. Evolve. Conquer.

Warchaic is a fast-paced online 1v1 strategy game where two civilizations clash across the ages. Build your economy, deploy your army, construct powerful defenses, and advance through history as you fight to destroy your opponent's base.

Lead Your Civilization Through the Ages

Begin with primitive warriors and gradually advance through different historical eras. Each new age unlocks new units, buildings, defenses, and strategic possibilities, constantly changing the battlefield.

Challenge Your Friends

Challenge your friends to private 1v1 battles and settle the score on the battlefield. Experiment with different civilizations and strategies, counter each other's tactics, and prove who is the better strategist.

Or take on other players online, adapt to unpredictable strategies, and fight your way to victory.

Build Your Economy

Gold and experience are the foundation of your civilization. Construct economic buildings, manage your resources, and decide whether to invest in your economy, strengthen your defenses, or spend everything on an offensive push.

Raise Your Army

Deploy melee fighters, ranged units, cavalry, and siege weapons onto a single, ever-changing frontline. Your units advance and fight automatically, leaving you to focus on army composition, timing, economy, and countering your opponent's strategy. Build the right army for the situation and adapt as the battle unfolds.

Choose Your Civilization

Different civilizations bring their own visual identity, units, buildings, and battlefield possibilities. Fight across history with civilizations such as the Romans, Egyptians, Aztecs, Ottomans, and more.

Shape Your Strategy

Buildings and defensive towers allow you to develop your side of the battlefield beyond simply producing units. Strengthen your economy, reinforce your defenses, and create a strategy that can survive your opponent's attacks.

Choose Powerful Cards

As the battle progresses, choose between powerful cards that can shape the rest of the match. Improve your economy, strengthen your troops, and create advantages that complement your strategy.

Destroy the Enemy Base

Every decision ultimately serves one goal: break through the enemy army and destroy their base before they destroy yours.

No two battles need to play out the same way. Adapt your army, economy, defenses, cards, and progression to overcome the strategy on the other side of the battlefield.

The Nine Realms are burning. From the green fields of Midgard to the golden gates of Asgard, hordes of raiders, berserkers, draugr and giants crash against your defenses - and every realm sends its own boss at the end.

A True Counter System

In Wardspire there is no single "best" tower. Five damage types meet enemy resistances: armored foes shrug off arrows, flyers soar over every ballista, the Völva heals her escort under fire. To hold the Nine Realms, you read your enemies - and build the right answer.

8 Towers, 16 Ways to Grow Them

From the Watchtower, Ballista, Runestone and Rime Totem to the Harpoon Thrower, Storm Pillar, Blight Totem and War Horn: every tower has a distinct role and two specialization paths at max level. Plus selectable target priorities per tower - from "first in line" to dedicated healer-hunting.

The Nine Realms of Norse Myth

9 hand-designed maps, each with its own biome, paths and rules: elven woods, dwarven mines, freezing mists, rivers of lava, the realm of the dead. Multiple portals and converging lanes raise the pressure - and in wave 20 the realm boss awaits, and it MUST be slain.

Permanent Progression: The Forge

Every victory earns Glory. In the Forge you unlock new towers, buy global upgrades and outfit each tower individually in the Armory. Losing is part of the plan: you come back stronger.

Features

  • 8 towers with 2 specializations each and 8 target priorities
  • 17 enemy types with resistances, abilities and elite ranks, including 9 realm bosses
  • 9 realms with multi-path lanes and free tower placement
  • Roguelite progression: Glory, the Forge, the Armory

Warring Kingdoms is a RPG centered on creating, ruling, and expanding fantasy kingdoms.

Unlike most RPGs, Warring Kingdoms features a complete large-scale battle system, allowing players to resolve military conflicts directly on the tabletop rather than through abstract narration.

The game combines kingdom management, tactical warfare, resource management, politics, and roleplaying into a single experience.

BUILD AND RULE YOUR KINGDOM

Create your kingdom and decide how it will develop.

Manage resources, raise armies, recruit characters, deal with political problems, explore the world, and make decisions that can affect the future of your realm.

Your kingdom is more than a place on the map. It is an evolving part of the campaign, shaped by the decisions of its rulers.

FIGHT LARGE-SCALE BATTLES

When kingdoms go to war, battles are played out on the tabletop using a dedicated large-scale combat system.

Command infantry, archers, cavalry, monsters, and other forces while dealing with the changing conditions of the battlefield.

Military conflicts are not reduced to a single dice roll or a simple narration of what happened. The battle itself becomes part of the game.

PLAY YOUR CHARACTER ON THE BATTLEFIELD

Commanders are not limited to moving units.

Characters can use their normal RPG abilities during battles, allowing players to take actions that go beyond conventional military tactics.

Cast spells.

Inspire your troops.

Negotiate with enemies.

Challenge enemy leaders to a duel.

Interact with the battlefield.

Find creative solutions to military problems.

The same RPG rules that govern your character outside of combat can become tools during a war.

MANAGE RESOURCES AND MAKE DIFFICULT DECISIONS

Every kingdom has limited resources.

Decide where to invest them and what risks are worth taking.

Raise new troops, support your population, prepare for war, explore dangerous territory, or strengthen your kingdom.

There is no single path to developing a successful realm.

POLITICS, DIPLOMACY AND CONFLICT

War is only one way to deal with other kingdoms.

Form alliances, negotiate agreements, respond to political events, impose decisions, and deal with the consequences of your actions.

The decisions made by rulers can change relationships between kingdoms and create conflicts that may last for an entire campaign.

A LIVING CAMPAIGN

Warring Kingdoms is designed around long-running tabletop campaigns.

Players control their kingdoms and characters while the narrator presents the world and its consequences.

Events can change the political landscape, kingdoms can rise or fall, and the outcome of one conflict can create the circumstances for the next.

Your decisions become part of the history of the campaign.

CREATE YOUR OWN HISTORY

Warring Kingdoms does not give you a predetermined story.

Build your kingdom.

Raise your armies.

Lead your characters.

Make alliances.

Fight your wars.

And decide what your kingdom will become.
